title: Sex and the City
full_review:
"Sex and the City" (New Line/HBO) is a frothy but morally flawed romantic comedy that updates the adventures of the world's most famous quartet of Cosmos drinkers.

Set four years after the end of the popular cable-TV series, the film finds columnist-turned-author Carrie Bradshaw (Sarah Jessica Parker) and her longtime boyfriend, known as Mr. Big (Chris Noth), purchasing a lavish apartment together and discussing the possibility of marriage.

Providing a good example for them are happily settled Charlotte (Kristin Davis) and her attentive hubby, Harry (Evan Handler). Exiled to Brooklyn, N.Y., and pressured by the demands of work and motherhood, Miranda (Cynthia Nixon) has been neglecting husband Steve (David Eigenberg). Freewheeling Samantha, meanwhile, has left the titular city altogether to live with and manage her actor boyfriend, Smith (Jason Lewis), as he establishes himself in Hollywood.

Conscientious themes of forgiveness and reconciliation as well as a generally positive view of marriage are swamped, in writer-director Michael Patrick King's adaptation, by errant materialism and an approach to human sexuality at once immature and indiscreet.

The film contains graphic sexual activity (some of it nonmarital and aberrant); rear, upper-female and partial nudity; sexual and scatological humor; two same-sex kisses; some rough and crude language; and two uses of profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
